subject: Delegated HIDE increment 2 -- the effectful-step approval round-trip
status: VERIFIED BY THE CONTROLLER. Tests re-run independently. Not merged pending one finding.

the_trap_was_avoided.hazard: Clearing pending_approval is what APPROVAL means -- do_paused sees None and resumes into Act. A denial implemented as a clear would run the effect the user just refused.
the_trap_was_avoided.outcome: Avoided. host.rs:6510 routes approve to approve_pending_effect; host.rs:6513 routes deny to deny_pending_effect.
the_trap_was_avoided.and_it_is_pinned: deny_effect_live_intent_skips_effect_and_does_not_hang asserts !target.exists() -- a real file that the effectful step would have written -- plus StepStatus::Skipped, a terminal phase (does not hang), and an approval.resolved(deny) event. Its comment names the bug class it kills.

tests_re_run_independently_by_controller.note: Run by name with --nocapture to confirm they executed rather than being silently filtered out, which a whole-suite pass count cannot distinguish.

design_accepted.chosen: Per-run ApprovalHub mailbox drained by the kernel-turn loop while paused, mirroring the existing InterruptHub.
design_accepted.why_it_is_right: No dependency edge from hide-kernel to hide-backend; AgentState stays solely owned by the driver; do_paused's existing idempotence makes a spurious wake harmless. It yields while parked (20ms sleep) rather than spinning, so a concurrent approve_effect can actually land instead of the run burning its max_steps budget in under a millisecond.
design_accepted.stale_decision_handling: A decision naming a step other than the pending one is ignored and the run keeps parking, so a late click on a previous step cannot resolve the current one.
design_accepted.self_approval_is_structurally_impossible: ApprovalDecision is only ever constructed from an explicit approve_effect/deny_effect intent, so a turn cannot approve its own effect.

findings.finding: step_id is optional on the wire. The intent handler parses payload.step_id into an Option<StepId> and deposits it as-is; ApprovalHub treats None as 'resolve whatever is pending' (targets_pending defaults to true). A client that omits step_id therefore creates a BLANKET approval, and because decisions are buffered, one deposited while nothing is pending will be applied to the next effectful step that pauses -- an effect the user may never have been shown.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the permission boundary. Everything else in the round-trip is careful precisely so that a human sees each effect before it runs; an optional step_id quietly reintroduces the case where one runs unseen. Not model-exploitable -- the host only deposits from an explicit human intent -- but a lazy or buggy client silently gets blanket approval.
findings.recommended_fix: Require step_id for approve_effect. Either reject the intent without one, or honour None only when a pause is ALREADY pending at deposit time, never for a buffered decision. Deny may safely keep the blanket form: a blanket deny is fail-safe.
findings.status: NOT FIXED -- raised for decision, since tightening a wire protocol is an API change.

findings.finding: Increment 1's two low findings (the dead `if n > 0 { let _ = n; }` block and `seed_code_file` visibility) were touched in services.rs (+6/-1). Not separately verified.

what_this_unblocks: The kernel path can now pause on an effectful step, be approved or denied through the live intent, and continue. That was the stated prerequisite for defaulting HIDE_KERNEL_TURN on, which in turn gates the Planner/Executor/Verifier loop, tool parse/run, mid-turn permissions and the deterministic oracles.
explicitly_not_done: HIDE_KERNEL_TURN default NOT flipped. That is a separate decision and it belongs to the user, not to a passing test.
Nothing merged to build/hide-impl-2026-07-19 or main.

The second prerequisite named in the gating comment -- answer surfacing -- is now exercised in combination with the pause by the approve test, but the comment above the flag should be updated or removed by whoever flips it, not left to contradict the code.
